text.p: Swiss shares closed more than one percent lower, but shares of Ciba Specialty Chemicals saw solid demand on their first day of trading.

Dealers said the easing U.S. dollar, a fall on U.S. and European bourses, as well as weakness in bonds, contributed to the market's slide. However, Ciba bucked the trend, ending at 116.50 francs, 6.50 francs above the initial flotation price of 110 francs in the global offering.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index lost 66.3 points, or 1.42 percent, to end at 4.609.9. and the all-share SPI fell 31.75 points to 2,922.70.
Dealers said Ciba had a successful start, hitting a day high of 118.0 francs. Foreign demand was said to be high.
Otherwise, investors seemed cautious about further interest rate development and some took profits, one trader noted.
"Insecurity is likely to last awhile," he added, referring to the U.S. Federal Reserve Board's meeting later this month.
Clariant, another specialty chemicals company, added four francs to close at 715. Electrowatt and EMS Chemie also firmed in the blue-chip segment.
ABB and SMH were lower but losses were held in check.
Novartis registered shares and Roche were among the more prominent losers of the day.
Novartis slid 32 francs to 1,756 and Roche gave up 225 francs to end at 12,255.
Banks were lower on a broad front. UBS gave up 16 francs to finish at 1,332. SBC was almost two percent lower, ending six francs off at 304. Insurers also mostly lost ground.
Swissair fell five francs to 1,289. But Adecco bucked the trend, adding three francs to close at 457.
